title: Far person, approaching
purpose: Small-in-frame recall at the longest sight line this room can offer, measured as an ACQUISITION RANGE rather than as a single yes/no at one distance. The person stands at the room's maximum axial depth (6.9 m, 44 px tall) until sim t = 18 s, then walks in at 0.25 m/s to 4.0 m (74 px), arriving at t = 29.6 s. The observable is the range at which the follower first confirms, plus how many times it flips while crossing the threshold. Re-fly this whenever preprocess.c changes: the Sep 11 resize study showed nearest-neighbour downscaling costs recall specifically on small people, and that cost shows up here as the acquisition range moving. If this scene is ever added to run_acceptance2.sh it needs a cell duration of at least 45 s: in the committed simv2 suite a 45 s cell's scored window ran sim t = 10.45-35.55 s, which contains the whole 18-29.6 s walk-in.

subjects.name: subj_person_target
subjects.note: Measured 2026-09-12 on the MATTE floor (the current default, floor_reflectance 0), champion float net through build_scene.py --preview's own preprocessing, camera on the drone eye line at (0, 0, 0.8) facing +x. Apparent height / confidence along this scene's own path: 6.9 m 44 px 0.701 | 6.5 m 47 px 0.654 | 6.0 m 51 px 0.853 | 5.5 m 55 px 0.906 | 5.0 m 60 px 0.959 | 4.5 m 66 px 0.925 | 4.0 m 74 px 0.933. The previous note here claimed 0.905 at 6.5 m; that number is REAL but was measured on the pre-Sep-12 reflective floor and reproduces exactly with --floor-reflectance 0.2. On the matte floor the same placement reads 0.654, i.e. the old note overstated this scene's target by about +0.25 confidence. x = 6.9 is the true maximum: the far wall's inner face is at x = 6.95 and the panel is 8 mm thick, leaving 46 mm of clearance. The old 6.5 was 0.4 m short of the maximum it claimed to be. MATTE 2026-09-14 re-measurement (the note above was already matte, dated 2026-09-12, but written against the 0.70 bar). Walk-in probe = camera fixed at the origin, the subject moved by its own drift joint to each x (the flown mechanism): 6.9 m 43 px 0.701 | 6.5 m 45 px 0.654 | 6.0 m 49 px 0.731 | 5.5 m 54 px 0.866 | 5.0 m 59 px 0.952 | 4.5 m 66 px 0.868 | 4.0 m 74 px 0.956 (float/clean; px by MuJoCo segmentation). 6.9 and 6.5 m reproduce the 09-12 numbers exactly; the interior points differ from the 09-12 list (0.853/0.906/0.959/0.925/0.933) by up to 0.12 because that list re-placed the card at each x, re-baking its background, whereas the drift joint carries the x = 6.9 card. Same walk-in on the other paths: chip/clean 0.801/0.768/0.693/0.890/0.941/0.864/0.958; float/himax 0.786/0.806/0.859/0.919/0.963/0.952/0.983; chip/himax 0.744/0.780/0.872/0.906/0.953/0.955/0.978. Against the shipped 0.75 bar: the 6.9 m static opening is BELOW the bar on float/clean (0.701) rather than 'exactly on' it, but ABOVE it on chip/clean (0.801) and on both himax paths (0.79 / 0.74), so which path is flown decides whether the opening confirms; 'confirm no later than ~6.0 m (0.853)' is not supported on the walk-in path (6.0 m reads 0.731 float/clean, 0.693 chip/clean, below 0.75); 'solid by 5.5 m' holds (0.866-0.919 on every probe). The structural limitation stands: 43-44 px is the smallest this room can draw the person. Bar: these notes were written against --vis-enter 0.70 on the 20%-reflective floor; 0.75 ships since 2026-09-13. [probe key: float/clean = champion float net via build_scene.py --preview preprocessing; chip = firmware preprocess + model_id_dory.onnx; himax = himax_typical camera, mean of 2 draws; single-subject probe = this cutout alone, static, straight ahead, camera on the eye line; full tables in docs/eval_results/2026-09-14-scene-notes]

prediction.rationale: The static opening - observed from the follower's first scored frame (sim t ~ 10 s, see the limitation below) until the walk-in starts at 18 s - sits exactly on the enter threshold: 0.701 measured against follow_person.py's --vis-enter 0.7, needing 3 consecutive frames. Whether the drone confirms at 6.9 m or waits for the walk-in is genuinely undecided and is what the scene is for. It should confirm no later than ~6.0 m (0.853) and be solid by 5.5 m (0.906). The failure mode to watch is chatter during the static opening, which confirm_transitions bounds. All of these are champion-float-net numbers from a static render; the flown path is the chip net through firmware_preprocess and will differ. MATTE 2026-09-14: the '0.701 ... exactly on the enter threshold' figure reproduces, but the bar is now 0.75, so on the float/clean path the opening sits 0.05 below it; chip/clean reads 0.801 at 6.9 m (above). 'No later than ~6.0 m (0.853)' -> 0.731 on the walk-in path; 'solid by 5.5 m (0.906)' -> 0.866, still above the bar. See the subject note. Bar: these notes were written against --vis-enter 0.70 on the 20%-reflective floor; 0.75 ships since 2026-09-13.

limitations: This scene CANNOT pose a decisive far-person question, and the reason is structural rather than a choice made here. Apparent height is set by the subject's AXIAL depth (x), not by Euclidean range - measured: a 1.7 m person at x = 6.9 renders 44 px tall for every y from 0 to 4.6 m, while the reported range grows 6.90 -> 8.29 m. Axial depth is capped by the far wall at x = 6.95 and by the drone's spawn, which is hardcoded as `-- 0,0` in run_sim_headless.sh and is the same for every scene. So the smallest the reference person can ever be, in any scene in this room, is ~44 px in the 244-px frame (23 px at the model's 128x128 input), where the champion float net reads 0.65-0.72 - straddling the 0.70 enter threshold, and NOT monotone in range (6.5 m 0.654, 6.6 m 0.662, 6.7 m 0.681, 6.8 m 0.716, 6.9 m 0.701, because the card's baked background changes with subject_x). Genuine small-in-frame recall collapse starts below ~35 px drawn (33 px -> 0.366, 28 px -> 0.280, and a 0.28 floor all the way down to 12 px), which needs >= 8.6 m of axial depth. Nothing editable in this file reaches it.

Two workarounds were built and measured, and both are rejected here rather than left as open options. (1) Shrinking height_m to fake distance is INVALID: at six matched drawn heights (32/34/36/38/40/42 px) a shrunk subject at 6.5 m reads 0.378/0.367/0.426/0.586/0.648/0.601 against 0.512/0.650/0.642/0.696/0.758/0.658 for the real 1.7 m person at the matching range - lower in 6 cases out of 6. The mechanism was not isolated - a shorter card sits lower in the frame relative to the 0.8 m eye line, and the two sets also differ in whole-frame composition and brightness (114-137 DN with the camera drawn back vs 146 DN at 6.5 m) - but whatever the cause, equal pixel height does not buy equal confidence, so height_m is not a usable stand-in for range. (2) Placing the person off-axis buys no smallness at the start (see above) and drops confidence to 0.377-0.583 at y = 2.0-4.6 m; and follow_person.py commands zero yaw while unconfirmed, so the drone would never turn toward a target it cannot confirm.

The fix that WOULD make a static far-person test possible is not in this file: spawn the drone near the back wall instead of at the origin. The room's interior runs x = -2.95 to 6.95, so a spawn at x = -2.8 gives 9.7 m of axial depth and a 30.5 px person - inside the collapse regime measured above - without touching the room or the subject. That is a run_sim_headless.sh change (and DRONE_START in build_scene.py, which only records it in the manifest). Reported, not made.

The gates above are declarative. scoreboard.py reads only expected_behaviour.target from the manifest; it does not evaluate expected_behaviour.gates, and commanded_motion_while_unconfirmed_m and confirm_transitions are not among the metrics it computes. s09 is also not in run_acceptance2.sh's CORE matrix, so this scene has never been flown.

t_start_s is on the SIMULATOR clock, not the follower's. The simulator - and this subject's drive law with it - is already running during process start-up and the drone's take-off, so the walk-in must be scheduled late enough that the static far-person phase is still there when scoring begins. Measured across all 13 committed runs in docs/sim_results/2026-09-11-simv2/runs (correlating each run's follow_log.csv wall clock against its truth.csv, which logs wall and sim time side by side), the follower's FIRST scored row lands at sim t = 8.65-10.90 s. t_start_s = 18.0 leaves roughly 8 s of observed hold at 6.9 m and is in line with the other drift scenes (s08 18 s, s14 22 s, s06b 25 s). An earlier start - 8.0 s, as in the first version of this fix - would have put the entire static phase before the first scored frame. Anything that changes sim start-up or take-off timing moves this window, so the observed hold length is approximate and should be read from the truth log.
